question: Should maintainers resolve the conflict and land this Codex lane-release fix with focused runner proof, or require live wedged app-server proof before merge?
rationale: The patch is a narrow fix for a real lane-release gap, but it deliberately changes when a timed-out Codex attempt releases same-session work and the current branch cannot merge cleanly.

options.title: Resolve conflict and land with focused proof
options.body: Rebase or manually resolve the branch, keep the lane-release hooks and regression test intact, rerun required checks, and accept the existing focused proof for this runner-owned contract.

options.title: Require live wedge proof
options.body: Pause merge until a live or Crabbox Codex app-server wedge demonstrates that late cleanup does not corrupt session state or message delivery.

options.title: Pause for broader recovery coordination
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want to coordinate the Codex lane fix with the separate WhatsApp final-error and diagnostic recovery surfaces first.

recommendation.title: Resolve conflict and land with focused proof
recommendation.body: Rebase or manually resolve the branch, keep the lane-release hooks and regression test intact, rerun required checks, and accept the existing focused proof for this runner-owned contract.
